title: Third party, repeaters and ITU regions
blurb: Third-party limits, 10 m repeaters, interference duties, ITU regions, and automatic digital stations.

G1E01.why: A third party whose license was **revoked and not reinstated** is disqualified. Citizenship and language do not matter.

G1E02.why: The 10 m repeater transmits on HF, so its control operator needs **General or higher**.
G1E02.trap: The Technician's input on 2 m is not the issue; the 10 m output is.

G1E03.why: Outside the auto-control segments, the station that **starts the contact** must be under local or remote control.

G1E04.why: A nearby FCC Monitoring Station, a secondary band and spread spectrum **each** call for steps to avoid interference.
G1E04.trap: Each condition on its own is correct, so all three apply.

G1E05.why: Messages must concern **amateur radio, personal remarks, or emergencies/disaster relief**.
G1E05.trap: Emergency-only and licensed-only limits are too narrow.

G1E06.why: North and South America are in **ITU Region 2**.

G1E07.why: There is **no part** of the 2.4 GHz band for communicating with non-licensed Wi-Fi stations.

G1E08.why: Spread spectrum is limited to **10 W PEP** output.

G1E10.why: A **propagation beacon** network operates on those frequencies, so avoid them.
G1E10.trap: These are beacons, not emergency or FCC bulletin frequencies.

G1E11.why: Auto-to-auto digital contact is allowed **anywhere on 6 m or shorter** and in limited HF segments.

G1E12.why: Third-party messages may go via remote control **whenever FCC rules allow them** at all.
